heading: Monday, April 14, 2025
topLine: AI search proposes gravitational-wave detector layouts that beat next-generation designs in simulation. Also: 2 model releases: Zhipu AI GLM-4-32B-0414 / GLM-Z1 and OpenAI GPT-4.1.

items.headline: AI search proposes gravitational-wave detector layouts that beat next-generation designs in simulation
items.summary: Mario Krenn's Artificial Scientist Lab at the Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light, with LIGO's Rana Adhikari and Yehonathan Drori, built Urania, which recast interferometer design as continuous optimisation and found topologies that could extend detectable range by more than an order of magnitude, some using mechanisms the authors say they do not yet fully understand. Published in Physical Review X with 50 designs released as a public 'Detector Zoo'; the designs are simulated, not built.

sources.name: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light

image.alt: Sketch of the Urania discovery engine optimising a pool of interferometer designs

items.headline: Zhipu AI releases GLM-4-0414 and GLM-Z1 reasoning models
items.summary: Zhipu released the open-weight GLM-4-32B-0414 series, including the GLM-Z1-32B and GLM-Z1-9B reasoning models and the GLM-Z1-Rumination deep-research model, alongside its new Z.ai domain. Zhipu claims GLM-Z1-32B matches DeepSeek-R1 on some tasks.

image.alt: GLM-4-32B-0414 benchmark scores compared with other models

items.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-4.1, 4.1 mini and 4.1 nano in the API
items.summary: The API-only GPT-4.1 family supports up to 1 million tokens of context. OpenAI reported 54.6% on SWE-bench Verified (versus 33.2% for GPT-4o) and gains in instruction following.
